Expands an open drop for a tuple by collecting each field place and subpath, creating the ladder bottom, and then building a field-drop ladder. It calls `tcx`, `field_subpath`, `drop_ladder_bottom`, and `drop_ladder`.

Finds the boxed value inside the nested `Box` representation, resolves the dereference subpath for that interior, and emits a drop for the pointee before outer box handling continues. It calls `tcx`, `deref_subpath`, and `drop_subpath`.

Expands an open drop for an ADT: empty ADTs become an unreachable block, unions and `ManuallyDrop` skip content drops, ordinary contents are handled by `open_drop_for_adt_contents`, boxes additionally drop their pointee via `open_drop_for_box_contents`, and ADTs with destructors route through `destructor_call_block`. It calls `patch`, `tcx`, `Unwind::is_cleanup`, `open_drop_for_adt_contents`, `destructor_call_block`, `Unwind::map`, and `open_drop_for_box_contents`.

Builds the content-dropping portion of an ADT open drop by first creating the ladder bottom, then using `move_paths_for_fields` plus `drop_ladder` for single-variant ADTs or delegating enums to `open_drop_for_multivariant`. It calls `drop_ladder_bottom`, `move_paths_for_fields`, `drop_ladder`, and `open_drop_for_multivariant`.

Builds variant-specific drop ladders for an enum, including separate unwind ladders when needed, and then dispatches on the discriminant to the appropriate variant drop path while handling otherwise/fallback cases. It calls `Unwind::is_cleanup`, `tcx`, `move_paths_for_fields`, `drop_halfladder`, `drop_ladder`, `param_env`, `goto_block`, `drop_block`, `adt_switch_block`, and `Unwind::map`.

Creates a block that reads the ADT discriminant into a temporary and switches to the prebuilt variant blocks, then guards that switch behind the relevant drop-flag test. It calls `tcx`, `patch`, and `drop_flag_test_block`.

Builds a MIR call block that invokes the type’s `Drop::drop` destructor on `self.place` via a mutable reference, then clears the shallow drop flag for the path at block entry and returns a guarding test block. Calls `new_temp`, `assign`, `drop_flag_test_block`, and uses `elaborator.clear_drop_flag` and `elaborator.patch().new_block`.

Constructs the basic-block loop that drops each indexed element of an array/slice range: one block computes the current element pointer and increments the index, another tests whether the loop is finished, and the drop terminator is patched to iterate or exit. Calls `new_temp`, `constant_usize`, and `assign`, and uses `elaborator.patch().new_block` plus `elaborator.patch().patch_terminator`.

Expands an open drop for arrays by analyzing which element subpaths are independently tracked; for fixed-size arrays it compresses contiguous droppable regions and preserved moved-out elements into a reverse drop ladder, otherwise it falls back to a loop-based strategy. Calls `drop_ladder_bottom`, `drop_ladder`, and `drop_loop_pair`, and uses `elaborator.array_subpath` to decide the plan.

Builds the entry/reset structure around `drop_loop` for slices or dynamically-sized array drops: creates temps for length and cursor, optionally builds an unwind-side loop, initializes the loop state, clears deep drop flags before iteration, and guards execution with a flag test. Calls `new_temp`, `drop_loop`, `constant_usize`, `assign`, `drop_flag_reset_block`, and `drop_flag_test_block`, and uses `elaborator.patch().new_block`.

Dispatches open-drop elaboration based on the place type: tuples/closure upvars/generator upvars go to tuple handling, ADTs to ADT-specific handling, trait objects to a full drop, fixed arrays to array handling, and slices to loop-based dropping. Calls `open_drop_for_tuple`, `open_drop_for_adt`, `complete_drop`, `open_drop_for_array`, and `drop_loop_pair`.
Creates a normal drop block for the whole place and then wraps it in a drop-flag test so the drop only runs when the path is considered present. Calls `drop_block` and `drop_flag_test_block`.

Creates a block that clears the path’s drop flag in the requested mode before continuing to `succ`, except on cleanup unwinds where the flag will never be read again and the successor is returned directly. Calls `new_block` and uses `elaborator.clear_drop_flag`.
Allocates a plain drop block and immediately elaborates that block in place, returning the block id for later wiring. Calls `drop_block` and `elaborate_drop`.
Builds a basic block whose terminator performs a MIR `Drop` of `self.place` to the given target with the given unwind behavior. Calls `new_block`.
Builds a basic block containing only a `Goto` terminator to the target, preserving the requested unwind cleanup classification. Calls `new_block`.

Chooses how to branch based on the path’s shallow drop style: return the unset target for dead paths, the set target for always-live paths, or emit a conditional block that tests the stored drop flag for conditional/open drops. Calls `new_block` and uses `elaborator.drop_style` plus `elaborator.get_drop_flag`.
Utility that allocates an empty MIR basic block with the supplied terminator and cleanup bit through the patcher. Uses `elaborator.patch().new_block`.
Allocates a new temporary local of the given type at the current source span through the MIR patch. Uses `elaborator.patch().new_temp`.
Constructs an `Operand::Constant` holding a `usize` literal for the current source span.
Constructs a MIR assignment statement from `lhs` to `rhs` using the current source info.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/elabora: Coordinates the ElaborateDrops MIR pass: gathers move data, calls `remove_dead_unwinds` to prune no-op drop unwinds, builds initialized/uninitialized dataflow results, constructs an `ElaborateDropsCtxt`, calls `ElaborateDropsCtxt::elaborate` to generate the patch, then applies the patch and runs `deref_finder`.

Scans cleanup drop terminators and removes unwind edges for drops proven to be no-ops by maybe-initialized analysis. It builds a `MaybeInitializedPlaces` cursor, checks drop children with `on_all_drop_children_bits`, and rewrites matching unwinds to `UnwindAction::Unreachable`.
Synchronizes both initialization cursors to just before a location by calling `seek_before_primary_effect` on `inits` and `uninits`.
Returns whether a move path may be initialized and may be uninitialized by calling `contains` on both `inits` and `uninits`.
Implements a no-op debug formatter that always returns `Ok(())`.
Returns the mutable MIR patch stored in the elaboration context.
Returns the MIR body from the elaboration context.
Returns the type context from the elaboration context.
Returns the parameter environment by calling `ElaborateDropsCtxt::param_env`.

Classifies a drop as `Dead`, `Static`, `Conditional`, or `Open` from initialization state. In shallow mode it calls `InitializationData::maybe_live_dead`; in deep mode it walks descendants with `on_all_drop_children_bits`, calling `tcx`, `body`, and `InitializationData::maybe_live_dead` for each child.

Clears synthesized drop flags for a path. In shallow mode it calls `ElaborateDropsCtxt::set_drop_flag`; in deep mode it walks descendants with `on_all_children_bits`, using `tcx`, `body`, `ElaborateDropsCtxt::move_data`, and `ElaborateDropsCtxt::set_drop_flag` on each child.
Finds the move-path child for a specific field by calling `ElaborateDropsCtxt::move_data` and `rustc_mir_dataflow::move_path_children_matching`.
Finds the move-path child for a specific array element constant index by calling `ElaborateDropsCtxt::move_data` and `rustc_mir_dataflow::move_path_children_matching`.
Finds the dereference child move path by calling `ElaborateDropsCtxt::move_data` and `rustc_mir_dataflow::move_path_children_matching`.
Finds the move-path child for a specific downcast variant by calling `ElaborateDropsCtxt::move_data` and `rustc_mir_dataflow::move_path_children_matching`.
Returns the operand used to read a synthesized drop flag by calling `ElaborateDropsCtxt::drop_flag` and mapping the resulting place to `Operand::Copy`.
Returns the move-data environment stored in the context.
Returns the parameter environment stored in the context.
Lazily allocates a boolean local for a move path's drop flag by calling `MirPatch::new_internal` through `get_or_insert_with`.
Returns the place for an already-created drop-flag local by mapping the stored local with `Place::from`.

Performs full drop elaboration setup and flag instrumentation. It calls `collect_drop_flags`, `elaborate_drops`, `drop_flags_on_init`, `drop_flags_for_fn_rets`, `drop_flags_for_args`, and `drop_flags_for_locs`, then returns the accumulated patch.

Finds drop paths that need runtime flags by visiting reachable drop terminators, syncing analysis state with `InitializationData::seek_before`, resolving paths with `ElaborateDropsCtxt::move_data`, querying liveness with `InitializationData::maybe_live_dead`, walking drop descendants with `on_all_drop_children_bits`, and calling `create_drop_flag` for children that may be both live and dead.

Rewrites reachable drop terminators into precise drop control flow. For each tracked drop it calls `InitializationData::seek_before`, resolves the move path with `ElaborateDropsCtxt::move_data`, computes unwind targets using patch helpers, and invokes `rustc_mir_dataflow::elaborate_drops::elaborate_drop`; untracked non-replace drops trigger a delayed bug.
Builds a boolean MIR constant `Rvalue` for the given span and value.
Emits an assignment to a synthesized drop flag if one exists for the path. It calls `constant_bool` to build the assigned value and `MirPatch::add_assign` to insert the write.
Initializes all synthesized drop flags to `false` at function entry by calling `constant_bool` once and emitting assignments with `MirPatch::add_assign` for every stored flag.

Marks call destinations as initialized on cleanup-return edges of calls with cleanup unwinds. It resolves the destination with `ElaborateDropsCtxt::move_data`, walks affected bits with `on_lookup_result_bits`, and calls `set_drop_flag` with `DropFlagState::Present`.
Applies entry-state drop-flag effects for function arguments by calling `rustc_mir_dataflow::drop_flag_effects_for_function_entry`, which in turn calls `set_drop_flag` for each affected path.

Applies non-drop location-based drop-flag updates across reachable original basic blocks. It calls `rustc_mir_dataflow::drop_flag_effects_for_location` for each statement/location, forwarding each effect to `set_drop_flag`; for certain call terminators it also resolves the destination with `ElaborateDropsCtxt::move_data`, walks bits with `on_lookup_result_bits`, and calls `set_drop_flag` to mark the return place present before the critical edge.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_mir_dataflow/src/move_pat: Constructs a MoveDataBuilder with empty move/init tables, creates the initial local-root move paths for all non-deref-temp locals, and initializes reverse lookup state. It explicitly calls MoveDataBuilder::new_move_path for each eligible local root.

Allocates a new MovePath node, links it into its parent’s child/sibling chain when a parent exists, and creates matching empty entries in the per-path move and init maps. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Resolves a MIR Place to a MovePathIndex by walking dereferences and projections, rejecting illegal move sources such as borrowed content, slices, indexed arrays, and ADTs with destructors, while collapsing union field accesses to the union base path. It explicitly calls Gatherer::add_move_path to intern any needed projected child move paths.

Looks up or creates a projected child move path under an existing base path in the reverse-lookup projection table. It explicitly calls MoveDataBuilder::new_move_path when the projection has not been interned yet.
Ensures path structure exists for a non-moving access and ignores invalid move-path errors. It explicitly calls Gatherer::move_path_for.

Finishes move-data construction, emits debug dumps of recorded moves and move paths, and returns either the completed MoveData or the accumulated errors. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Entry point that builds a MoveDataBuilder, seeds argument initializations, walks every statement and terminator in the body, and returns the finalized move data. It explicitly calls MoveDataBuilder::new, MoveDataBuilder::gather_args, MoveDataBuilder::gather_statement, MoveDataBuilder::gather_terminator, and MoveDataBuilder::finalize.
Records each function argument as a deep initialization at entry and stores the init in the per-path init map. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.
Delegates statement processing for the current location to a Gatherer. It explicitly calls Gatherer::gather_statement.
Delegates terminator processing for the current location to a Gatherer. It explicitly calls Gatherer::gather_terminator.

Processes a MIR statement to update move-path, move, and initialization facts: it handles CopyForDeref bookkeeping, assignment destinations and their initialization kind, fake reads, and StorageDead moves while ignoring statement kinds that do not affect move tracking. It explicitly calls Gatherer::create_move_path, Gatherer::gather_init, Gatherer::gather_rvalue, and Gatherer::gather_move.

Scans an Rvalue and records moves from any operands it consumes, while ignoring non-moving forms such as references, address-of, discriminants, lengths, and nullary ops. It explicitly calls Gatherer::gather_operand.

Processes a MIR terminator to record operand moves and destination initializations for control-flow constructs such as Assert, SwitchInt, Yield, Call, and InlineAsm, while ignoring terminators that do not affect move tracking. It explicitly calls Gatherer::gather_operand, Gatherer::create_move_path, and Gatherer::gather_init.
Handles an operand by ignoring constants and copies and treating Operand::Move as a real move. It explicitly calls Gatherer::gather_move for move operands.

Records a move from a place, including special expansion of subslice patterns into disjoint constant-index element moves, and reports illegal move errors when path resolution fails. It explicitly calls Gatherer::move_path_for, Gatherer::record_move, and Gatherer::add_move_path.
Appends a MoveOut for the current location and indexes it by both move path and source location. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Records an initialization for a place at the current statement location, normalizing assignments to union fields so the union base path is marked initialized instead. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/reveal_: Checks whether the `RevealAll` MIR pass should run. It calls `mir_opt_level` on the session and also calls `super::inline::Inline.is_enabled` as an alternative enabling condition.

Executes the `RevealAll` pass on a MIR body unless the body is a generator. It calls `is_some` to detect generators, calls `def_id` and `param_env_reveal_all_normalized` to build the post-analysis typing environment, and then calls `visit_body_preserves_cfg` on `RevealAllVisitor` to rewrite the body without changing control flow.
Returns the visitor's stored `TyCtxt`. It does not call other methods from the provided methods list.

Visits a MIR constant and tries to normalize its literal under the visitor's typing environment, updating it only on success so impossible where-clauses are tolerated. It calls `try_normalize_erasing_regions`.

Visits a MIR type and tries to normalize it under the visitor's typing environment, replacing the type only when normalization succeeds so impossible where-clauses are tolerated. It calls `try_normalize_erasing_regions`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_middle/src/mir/tcx.rs::im: Constructs a `PlaceTy` from a plain type by storing the type and clearing any downcast variant information (`variant_index: None`).

Computes the type of a field projected from this place type, selecting the appropriate ADT variant when downcasted or indexing into tuple elements; it does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.
Computes the type of a single place projection using default callbacks and an empty param environment; explicitly calls `PlaceTy::projection_ty_core`.

Implements the core typing rules for MIR projection elements, handling deref, indexing, subslicing, downcast, field, and opaque-cast projections while preserving or updating downcast state; explicitly calls `PlaceTy::from_ty` when producing projected place types.

Computes a place type from a local plus projection chain by starting from the local declaration type and folding each projection element over it; explicitly calls `PlaceTy::from_ty` and `PlaceTy::projection_ty`.
Computes this `Place`'s type from local declarations and `TyCtxt`; explicitly calls `Place::ty_from`.
Computes this `PlaceRef`'s type from local declarations and `TyCtxt`; explicitly calls `Place::ty_from`.

Computes the result type of each MIR `Rvalue` form, delegating to operand, place, and operator typing for uses, references, pointer formation, arithmetic, aggregates, and box initialization. Explicitly calls `Operand::ty`, `Place::ty`, `BorrowKind::to_mutbl_lossy`, and `BinOp::ty`.
Classifies rvalue initialization as shallow only for `ShallowInitBox` and deep for all other rvalues; it does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.
Returns the type of an operand by reading the referenced place type for `Copy`/`Move` operands or the literal type for constants; explicitly calls `Place::ty`.

Determines the result type of a MIR binary operator, yielding the operand type for arithmetic/bitwise operations, the left-hand type for shifts and pointer offset, and `bool` for comparisons; it does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.
Converts MIR borrow kinds into HIR mutability, mapping mutable borrows to `Mut` and shared or shallow borrows to `Not`; it does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.

Maps MIR binary operators to their corresponding HIR binary operator kinds, rejecting unchecked and offset-only MIR operators as unreachable; it does not call other methods from the provided Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_analysis/src/collect/: Finds hidden-type constraints for a type-alias `impl Trait` by computing its defining HIR scope and traversing that scope with `TaitConstraintLocator`, using `walk_toplevel_module` for crate scope or explicitly calling `visit_item`, `visit_impl_item`, `visit_trait_item`, or `visit_foreign_item` on the defining node so sibling defining uses are included. It then cross-checks the chosen hidden type against collected `typeck_types` via `build_mismatch_error`, and reports an unconstrained opaque if nothing constrained it.

Per-item constraint checker for TAIT/associated opaque discovery: it skips items without typeck results, rejects `_`-inferred function returns by creating an error type, reads `typeck` results, filters `concrete_opaque_types` down to the target opaque, records typeck-visible hidden types, validates the item against `opaque_types_defined_by`, and then uses `mir_borrowck` to obtain the region-precise hidden type. When multiple defining uses disagree, it reports the mismatch with `build_mismatch_error` and updates or preserves `self.found` accordingly.
Returns the HIR map from `self.tcx.hir()` so `TaitConstraintLocator` can recursively traverse nested HIR nodes.
Visits expressions for TAIT constraint discovery; when it sees a closure, it calls `TaitConstraintLocator::check` on the closure's `def_id`, then continues traversal with `intravisit::walk_expr`.

Visits an item in the TAIT reveal scope, skipping the opaque item itself; for every other item it calls `TaitConstraintLocator::check` on the item's `def_id` and then recurses with `intravisit::walk_item`.
Visits an impl item during TAIT constraint search, skips the opaque item itself, calls `TaitConstraintLocator::check` on other impl items, and then continues with `intravisit::walk_impl_item`.
Visits a trait item for TAIT constraint collection by calling `TaitConstraintLocator::check` on the trait item's `def_id` and then recursing with `intravisit::walk_trait_item`.

Computes the hidden type for a return-position `impl Trait` by first scanning `typeck(owner_def_id).concrete_opaque_types` for the target opaque, normalizing each candidate with `remap_generic_params_to_declaration_params`, and using `build_mismatch_error` to stash HIR-level inconsistencies. It then queries `mir_borrowck(owner_def_id)` for the authoritative hidden type and, if present, traverses the owner body with `intravisit::walk_item`, `walk_impl_item`, or `walk_trait_item` using `RpitConstraintChecker` so nested bodies can be checked for mismatching constraints; otherwise it returns an error or diverging default type.

Checks one nested body for RPIT consistency by reading `mir_borrowck(def_id).concrete_opaque_types`, filtering to the target opaque, and comparing each discovered hidden type against `self.found`; on disagreement it reports the mismatch via `build_mismatch_error` and emits the diagnostic.
Returns `self.tcx.hir()` as the nested visit map so `RpitConstraintChecker` can traverse nested HIR structure.
Visits expressions while checking RPIT constraints; for closures it calls `RpitConstraintChecker::check` on the closure's `def_id`, then continues traversal with `intravisit::walk_expr`.
Visits an item in RPIT checking, skipping the opaque item itself; for every other item it calls `RpitConstraintChecker::check` on the item's `def_id` and then recurses with `intravisit::walk_item`.
Visits an impl item during RPIT checking, skips the opaque item itself, calls `RpitConstraintChecker::check` on other impl items, and continues traversal with `intravisit::walk_impl_item`.
Visits a trait item for RPIT checking by calling `RpitConstraintChecker::check` on the trait item's `def_id` and then recursing with `intravisit::walk_trait_item`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_infer/src/infer/opaque_ty: Scans a foldable value for local opaque aliases that are currently definable in this context, replaces each eligible opaque with a fresh inference type variable, and accumulates the resulting obligations. It first short-circuits when `next_trait_solver` is enabled or `has_opaque_types` is false, and for each matched opaque it calls `opaque_type_origin` to decide eligibility and `handle_opaque_type` to relate the new inference variable back to the opaque definition.

Handles the relation between an opaque type and another type during inference, ignoring error types, orienting the comparison by `a_is_expected`, and only treating local opaque aliases as definitional when they are valid for the current `DefiningAnchor`. When the opaque is allowed to be defined here, it calls `opaque_type_origin` to validate the defining context and then calls `register_hidden_type` to record the inferred hidden type; otherwise it emits diagnostics for invalid defining-use situations such as problematic opaque-to-opaque cases.

Resolves the concrete hidden type, computes the invariant lifetime arguments of the opaque plus `'static` as the allowed choice set, and visits the hidden type to constrain every free region to one of those choices. It calls `member_constraint` through the region visitor callback for each discovered region.

Determines whether a local opaque type is being defined from the current defining-use anchor and, if so, returns its `OpaqueTyOrigin`. For type-alias opaques it checks associated-type definitions via `opaque_types_defined_by` and otherwise calls `may_define_opaque_type` to decide whether the current item may define the opaque.
Visits inside binders without stopping, delegating traversal to `super_visit_with` and then continuing.
Processes each encountered region for opaque-member checking, skipping bound regions and invoking the stored callback for all other regions.

Traverses only types that contain free regions and selectively visits the parts relevant for opaque lifetime constraints. It skips enclosing-item lifetimes for closures and coroutines by manually visiting captured/upvar and signature-related components, visits only non-bivariant arguments of nested opaque aliases, and otherwise falls back to `super_visit_with`.
Returns whether this `UseKind` represents a defining use, yielding true for `DefiningUse` and false for `OpaqueUse`.

Registers an inferred hidden type for an opaque definition and produces the obligations needed to justify it. It calls `insert_hidden_type` to store or unify the hidden type in the opaque-type table, then calls `add_item_bounds_for_hidden_type` to add the opaque item's declared bounds as obligations on that hidden type.

Inserts a hidden type candidate into inference state for an opaque key. In intercrate mode it adds an ambiguous obligation instead of defining the opaque; otherwise it registers the hidden type in the opaque storage, and if a previous hidden type was already present it calls `eq_exp` to equate the old and new hidden types and extends the obligation list with the resulting obligations.

Instantiates the explicit bounds declared on an opaque item, rewrites them so they apply to the inferred hidden type, and pushes each rewritten predicate as an obligation. While folding each predicate, it calls `infer_projection` to replace eligible projection aliases with inference variables, and it substitutes self-references to the same opaque alias with `hidden_ty` before creating obligations.
Checks whether a named opaque type may be defined from the given local item by walking up the HIR parent chain from the item to see whether it reaches the opaque type’s defining scope.

method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_typeck/src/pat.rs::im: Builds an `ObligationCause` for pattern checking from `TopInfo`, marking whether the pattern originated from an expression, then delegates to `self.cause`. It does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.

Creates a pattern-specific type-equality diagnostic for `expected` versus `actual` using `pattern_cause`, and, when the pattern comes from an origin expression, augments the diagnostic with a function-call suggestion if the expression result could equal the actual type. Calls `pattern_cause`.
Emits a pattern type-equality error if one exists by obtaining a diagnostic from `demand_eqtype_pat_diag` and emitting it. Calls `demand_eqtype_pat_diag`.
Top-level entry point for pattern type checking: packages the expected type and origin into `TopInfo`, seeds initial `PatInfo`, and recursively type-checks the pattern. Calls `check_pat`.

Core recursive dispatcher for pattern type checking. It pre-resolves path patterns, computes the adjustment mode with `calc_adjust_mode`, applies match-ergonomics/default binding rules with `calc_default_binding_mode`, then dispatches by `PatKind` to specialized checkers and records the final type. Calls `calc_adjust_mode`, `calc_default_binding_mode`, `check_pat_lit`, `check_pat_range`, `check_pat_ident`, `check_pat_tuple_struct`, `check_pat_path`, `check_pat_struct`, `check_pat` (for or-pattern alternatives), `check_pat_tuple`, `check_pat_box`, `check_pat_deref`, `check_pat_ref`, and `check_pat_slice`.

Applies the chosen adjustment policy to the expected type and current default binding mode: passes through unchanged, resets to the initial binding mode, or peels references for match ergonomics. Calls `peel_off_references`.

Determines whether a pattern should preserve references, reset binding modes, or peel references before deeper checking, based on pattern kind, default-binding-mode availability, literal/reference behavior, and resolved path kind. It does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.

Repeatedly strips leading reference layers from the expected scrutinee type, updates the default binding mode to the corresponding by-reference mode, and records pattern adjustments for later lowering. It does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.

Type-checks a literal pattern, with special handling for byte-string and string-deref patterns, then enforces that the literal pattern type is a subtype of the expected type using a pattern-specific cause. Calls `pattern_cause`.

Type-checks range pattern endpoints, first ensuring each endpoint is numeric/char-like for better diagnostics, then unifying each side with the expected type and rejecting invalid or unresolved range types. Calls `emit_err_pat_range`, `demand_eqtype_pat_diag`, and `endpoint_has_type`.
Adds a diagnostic label describing an endpoint’s type when that type is not already erroneous. It does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.

Builds and emits the dedicated error for non-numeric/non-`char` range patterns, choosing the most relevant span, labeling failing endpoints, optionally labeling the other endpoint’s type, and attaching a teaching note. Calls `endpoint_has_type`.

Type-checks a binding pattern by determining and recording its binding mode, deriving the bound variable type from that mode, equating it with the local variable type, checking consistency across alternatives, and recursively checking any subpattern. Calls `demand_eqtype_pat`, `check_binding_alt_eq_ty`, and `check_pat`.

Ensures that the same binding introduced through pattern alternatives has the same type everywhere; when it does not, it builds a diagnostic, labels the first introduction site, explains the rule, and suggests adding or removing `ref` when appropriate. Calls `demand_eqtype_pat_diag` and `suggest_adding_missing_ref_or_removing_ref`.

Adds a targeted diagnostic suggestion to insert `ref` or remove `ref` when the expected and actual binding types differ only by a reference layer and the binding annotation matches that fix. It does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.

Constructs diagnostics suggesting how to rewrite `&`/`&mut` binding patterns into more idiomatic borrowed or mutable binding syntax depending on the enclosing pattern context. It does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.

Rejects dereference patterns that would implicitly dereference a trait object binding, emitting E0033 with an explanatory note, and otherwise accepts the pattern as dereferenceable. It does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.

Type-checks a struct pattern by resolving and validating the struct path, checking the resolved struct type against the expected type, then type-checking and validating the field subpatterns. Calls `check_pat` (when path resolution fails while walking fields), `demand_eqtype_pat`, and `check_struct_pat_fields`.

Type-checks a path pattern that must resolve to a unit constructor or constant: it validates the resolution kind, instantiates the value path, and checks the resulting pattern type against the expected type, emitting a specialized diagnostic on mismatch. Calls `pattern_cause` and `emit_bad_pat_path`.
